device.category: 8-voice polyphonic analogue synthesizer with split and dual keyboard modes, arpeggiator and patch memory

sources.title: Roland, 'JUPITER-8: Technical Specifications' (support article)

architecture.polyphony_mode: polyphonic, 8 voices; split; dual (4 voices, two patches per key); unison and solo
architecture.patch_memory_note: 64 patch memories and 8 patch presets (which also store split, arpeggio, hold, portamento, modulation and assign settings); tape dump.
architecture.summary: Two VCOs per voice: VCO-1 (triangle, saw, pulse, square, 16'-2') with cross modulation from VCO-2 (sine, saw, pulse, noise, chromatic range, low-frequency mode, fine tune, sync). A non-resonant HPF feeds a resonant low-pass VCF switchable between 12 and 24 dB/oct. Two ADSRs with key follow, one LFO with delay, and a performance LFO. Whole, split and dual key modes, four assign modes, arpeggiator, portamento, auto-tune, separate upper and lower outputs, and a highest-note CV and gate out.

modules.name: Keyboard and assigner
modules.panel_section: MEMORY PANEL: KEY MODE / ASSIGN / ARPEGGIO / GLIDE
modules.description: 61-key keyboard. KEY MODE splits or layers the voices into upper and lower patches; ASSIGN chooses how keys take voices; an arpeggiator and portamento act per section. Sends pitch CV and gates to the voices.

modules.name: LFO
modules.description: Main programmable LFO, shared by the voices, with delay.

modules.name: Performance LFO
modules.description: Second LFO for performance vibrato and growl, brought in by the LFO MOD button.

modules.name: VCO-1
modules.description: First oscillator; receives cross modulation from VCO-2.

modules.name: VCO-2
modules.description: Second oscillator; a LOW setting turns it into a low-frequency modulator for cross modulation.

modules.name: ENV-1
modules.description: ADSR with key follow and polarity; drives VCO modulation, PWM, cross mod and optionally the VCF.

modules.name: ENV-2
modules.description: ADSR with key follow; drives the VCA and optionally the VCF.

modules.name: VCA
modules.description: Shapes each voice with ENV-2, with LFO tremolo.

modules.name: Bender
modules.description: Left-right bender lever with separate VCO and VCF amounts.

modules.name: Patch memory and presets
modules.description: Patch memories, patch presets (a patch or split pair plus performance modes), manual panel, write, protect, tape memory and auto-tune.

modules.name: HPF
modules.description: Non-resonant high-pass filter ahead of the VCF.

modules.name: VCF (low-pass)
modules.description: Resonant low-pass, 12 or 24 dB/oct, with envelope, LFO and key follow.

properties.chip: IR3109 (shared with the Juno-6/60, per secondary sources)

modules.name: Highest note CV/gate
modules.description: Pitch CV and gate for the highest note played, for an external synthesizer.

modules.name: Output
modules.description: Upper, lower and mix outputs, balanced and unbalanced, and headphones.

behaviours.name: Key modes
behaviours.rule: WHOLE: one patch over 8 voices. SPLIT: upper and lower patches each side of a split point. DUAL: two patches layered on each key, 4-voice polyphony. BALANCE mixes the sections; each has its own output as well as MIX. In split the arpeggio plays the lower section only.

behaviours.name: Assign modes
behaviours.rule: SOLO (mono), UNISON (all voices on the played notes), POLY-1 and POLY-2 (one voice per key; POLY-2 suits portamento, as on the Jupiter-6).
behaviours.note: POLY-1/POLY-2 difference carried over from the Jupiter-4 and Jupiter-6 manuals.

behaviours.name: Arpeggio
behaviours.rule: UP, DOWN, U&D (last note of UP is first of DOWN) or RANDOM over 1-4 octaves, 1-20 Hz or from an external or DIN clock.

behaviours.name: Patch presets
behaviours.rule: 8 patch presets store a patch or split/dual pair together with key split, arpeggio, hold, portamento, modulation and assign settings.

behaviours.name: Cross modulation and sync
behaviours.rule: VCO-2 modulates VCO-1's frequency. SYNC resets VCO-2 from VCO-1. LOW FREQ makes VCO-2 a modulator whose pitch no longer follows the keys, set by its range control.

behaviours.name: Envelope key follow
behaviours.rule: With KEY FOLLOW on, attack, decay and release lengthen on lower notes and shorten on higher ones.

behaviours.name: Performance controls
behaviours.rule: The bender moves VCO-1 and/or VCO-2 and the VCF by their sensitivities. The LFO MOD button brings in a second LFO, rising over RISE TIME, to VCO and/or VCF.

behaviours.name: Highest-note CV
behaviours.rule: The rear CV and gate follow the highest note held, to play a monophonic synth alongside.

midi.note: No MIDI on the original. Later units have DCB (serial 282880 on); MIDI came only by retrofit.

LFO waveform order on the panel
source_inconsistencies: The PLUG-OUT lists LFO waveforms sine, triangle, saw, square and two randoms; Roland Australia and Polynominal give sine, saw, square and random; Vintage Synth Explorer gives sine, triangle, ramp and random.
Vintage Synth Explorer gives VCO-1 and VCO-2 the same four waveforms plus noise on VCO-2; Roland Australia, Arturia and the PLUG-OUT put sine (not square or triangle) on VCO-2.
Arpeggio range is 1-4 octaves in Roland's specifications; Roland Australia says it is switchable over 5 octaves.

modelling_gaps.detail: Not modelled: velocity sensitivity, effects, tempo sync, CONDITION and CIRCUIT MOD, LFO key trigger and TRIG ENV, octave buttons, key hold, bend gain, separate VCO-1/VCO-2 bend and mod switching on the lever panel, MONO assign.
An original owner's manual would settle the LFO and VCO-2 waveforms, envelope behaviour and memory procedures.
Early and later units, and the MKS-80 Rev 5, use different VCO, VCA and filter circuits.
